1: # OpenGlimpse — Project Documentation
2: # SCCCI Delegation Real-Time Facial Recognition Attendance System
3: # Problem Statement #10 | 4-Person Team
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 1. Project Overview
8: 
9: SCCCI (Singapore Chinese Chamber of Commerce & Industry) manages overseas business delegations of 15–30 (sometimes 100+) participants across multiple coaches and venues. Currently, headcount is taken manually by counting heads and doing roll calls — a slow, error-prone process that causes anxiety and programme overruns when someone is missing.
10: 
11: This system digitises and accelerates that process using a React-based mobile-first application with facial recognition as the primary attendance mechanism, supplemented by QR code scanning as a backup.
12: 
13: ---
14: 
15: ## 2. Use Case Definition
16: 
17: ### 2.1 Primary Use Case
18: **Title:** Real-Time Facial Recognition Attendance with Multi-Staff Sync
19: 
20: **Goal:** Allow SCCCI secretariat staff to take attendance for an overseas delegation in under 1 minute (30 pax) or 2 minutes (100+ pax) using facial recognition, with instant visibility of who is present or absent — across multiple staff devices simultaneously.
21: 
22: **Actors:**
23: - Staff / Secretariat (Primary) — takes attendance using facial recognition; can manually confirm identity if needed
24: - Trip Manager / Admin (Primary) — creates programmes, assigns staff, views consolidated real-time attendance, confirms departure readiness
25: - Delegate (Secondary) — identified via facial recognition as they enter coaches or venues
26: 
27: ### 2.2 Preconditions
28: - A programme has been created with a predetermined participant list
29: - Each delegate's facial photograph has been registered in the system (passport-sized photo)
30: - At least one staff member has the app open, is logged in, and is assigned to the current programme/route
31: - Internet connectivity (cellular data or hotspot) is available at the location for real-time cloud sync
32: - For first login by staff, updated facial photo is required to verify identity
33: 
34: ### 2.3 Main Flow (Happy Path)
35: 1. Admin creates a new programme with routes, bus assignments, and participant list.
36: 2. Staff member logs in with their account (verified by facial recognition on first login).
37: 3. Staff opens the attendance marking screen for their assigned route/coach.
38: 4. Delegate boards; staff activates live camera with facial detection. App displays bounding boxes around detected faces in real time.
39: 5. App matches detected face against stored delegate embeddings. If match confidence is high, delegate is marked Present automatically.
40: 6. If confidence is low or face is unrecognised, admin receives in-app alert. Staff can manually confirm identity from the list or use QR code backup.
41: 7. Attendance record syncs instantly to the cloud. All staff devices update in real time.
42: 8. The dashboard shows: Present list (with photos), Unidentified/Absent list (highlighted at top), and Ready-to-Depart status.
43: 9. When all delegates are accounted for, the Trip Manager confirms departure readiness.
44: 
45: ### 2.4 Alternative & Exception Flows
46: 
47: **Alt A — Low confidence facial match:**
48: - App flags confidence score and shows top candidate matches.
49: - Staff taps to confirm or manually selects from the list.
50: - Fallback: QR code scan on separate tab if delegate has badge.
51: 
52: **Alt B — Unidentified face:**
53: - Admin receives in-app alert for faces that don't match any registered delegate.
54: - Staff can manually add the person if it's a new arrival or late joiner.
55: - Photo quality may be poor — staff can request re-scan or use QR/manual override.
56: 
57: **Alt C — Manual attendance override:**
58: - Staff can always tap a delegate's name from the list to mark them Present or Absent.
59: - Covers roll calls when facial recognition is not available or delegate forgot badge.
60: 
61: **Alt D — Delegate joins/leaves programme mid-journey:**
62: - Admin amends the programme participant list on-the-fly from the app (add/remove delegate, change route/coach assignment).
63: 
64: **Alt E — Offline when scanning:**
65: - App queues facial scans locally (face image + embedding) if internet drops.
66: - When connectivity restores, queued scans are sent to backend for processing.
67: - Cloud data merges offline scans without loss or duplication.
68: 
69: ---
70: 
71: ## 3. System Requirements (Prioritised)
72: 
73: P1 = must-have MVP; P2 = high value, build after P1; P3 = nice-to-have.
74: 
75: | Pri. | Requirement | Owner |
76: |------|-------------|-------|
77: | P1 | Facial recognition with real-time face detection — bounding boxes drawn around faces in camera view | Ryan |
78: | P1 | Face embedding generation & storage — store delegate faces as embeddings in PostgreSQL | Ryan + Backend |
79: | P1 | Manual identity confirmation — staff can manually tap delegate name to override low-confidence matches | Ryan / XY |
80: | P1 | Offline sync queue — frontend buffers facial scans locally; backend processes & merges on reconnect | Rayhan |
81: | P1 | Real-time attendance dashboard with present/absent/unidentified lists; missing marked at top | XY |
82: | P1 | Multi-staff cloud sync — all staff see the same attendance in real time across devices | Backend + Ryan |
83: | P1 | Programme & route creation — admin can set up trips, assign buses/routes, manage participant lists | XY / Matt |
84: | P1 | Staff account management — admin CRUD operations, staff login, face verification on first login | Matt |
85: | P1 | In-app alerts for unidentified faces — admin notified of FR matches below confidence threshold | Ryan / Backend |
86: | P1 | China-accessible hosting — app must not be blocked by Great Firewall | Backend |
87: | P2 | QR code backup scanning — delegate has QR on badge; staff can switch tab to scan if FR not possible | Ryan |
88: | P2 | Attendance summary & data aggregation — totals, pass rates, missing delegates report | XY |
89: | P2 | Ready-to-depart indicator — admin confirms all delegates accounted for before departure | XY |
90: | P2 | In-app chat & announcements — team members can communicate; announce updates with reactions | Rayhan |
91: | P2 | AI chatbot assistant — context-aware chatbot that answers programme questions via Groq API; triggered by @assistant prefix in chat | Backend |
92: | P2 | Navbar navigation — easy routing between Programme, Attendance, Profile, Chat sections | Rayhan |
93: | P3 | User profile management — staff can update personal info including new facial photo | Matt |
94: 
95: ---
96: 
97: ## 4. Tech Stack Details
98: 
99: ### 4.1 Frontend
100: - React web application with responsive design — optimised for staff smartphones and tablets
101: - Facial recognition: face-api.js library for real-time face detection, embedding generation, and similarity matching
102: - Camera API: device camera access with live face detection and bounding box visualization
103: - QR code scanner: separate tab with camera-based QR decoding (backup mode)
104: - Offline queue: browser localStorage for queuing facial scans and embeddings when disconnected
105: - UI: simple, high-contrast, glanceable — unidentified/absent delegates surfaced at top of list
106: - Chat auto-scroll: chat snaps to the latest message on first entry and when already at the bottom on new messages; a floating jump-to-bottom button (with unread count) appears when scrolled up
107: 
108: ### 4.2 Backend
109: - Node.js REST API (Express.js) for programmes, routes, attendance, user management, and chat
110: - Real-time sync: WebSockets (Socket.io) for instant multi-device attendance updates, in-app chat, and message reactions
111: - AI chatbot: Groq API (llama-3.3-70b-versatile) with full programme context; chatbot user seeded in DB; triggered by configurable prefix (e.g. `@assistant`) in chat
112: - Database: PostgreSQL — stores programmes, participants, facial embeddings (vectors), scan events, chat messages, user accounts
113: - Offline queue processing: backend receives offline scans, validates embeddings, and merges with live data without duplication
114: - Auth: staff login via JWT; delegate identity verified by facial embedding similarity
115: - Hosting: must be accessible from China — Alibaba Cloud (Singapore/Hong Kong region) strongly preferred
116: 
117: ### 4.3 Data & Privacy
118: - Delegate data: name, facial photograph (passport-sized JPEG), optional QR code ID, optional NFC tag ID
119: - Facial embeddings: stored in PostgreSQL as numeric vectors (face-api.js output); compared for similarity matching
120: - Staff data: account credentials, facial photo for login verification, permission levels
121: - Photos pre-registered by admin before the programme; staff updates own photo on first login
122: - Chat messages: retained for programme history; can be archived per admin policy
123: - Message reactions: one reaction per user per message (WhatsApp-style emoji); stored in `message_reactions` keyed on `(message_id, user_id)`; synced live over the `/chat` socket namespace via the `react` event and `reaction:update` broadcasts
124: 
125: ### 4.4 Offline Sync Engine
126: 
127: #### Architecture
128: - **Client:** Dexie.js (IndexedDB) with `requestCache` and `pendingChanges` tables
129: - **Interception layer:** `services/api.js` `request()` caches GET responses; offline reads serve from cache, offline writes queue `{ method, path, body, token }` to `pendingChanges`
130: - **Auth endpoints:** `/api/auth` and `/api/user` in `SYNC_PREFIXES`; login excluded via `NEVER_QUEUE`; token carried in ops for auth writes
131: - **Sync trigger:** `hooks/useSync.js` calls `sync/changeHandler()` on mount, `online` event, and tab `focus`; dispatches `sync:start` before flushing and `sync:done` after (in `finally`, so it also fires on failure) to drive the syncing indicator and `pendingCount` refresh
132: - **Server:** `POST /sync` registered in `index.js` via `registerSyncRoutes(app)`; handled by `modules/sync/syncController.js` which replays ops against Sequelize models; auth ops validated via `parseToken()` + DB lookup
133: - **Vite proxy:** `/sync` added to `vite.config.js` proxy table so `changeHandler` fetch reaches Express (was root cause of silent sync failure)
134: - **Synced entity types:** programme, route, delegate, attendance (single + batch), readyToDepart, auth, face upload (`PATCH /api/user/:id/face/default`); batch attendance pulls `programmeId` from the URL path since the client payload only carries `records`
135: - **Not synced:** login (`/api/auth/login`); face recognition (`/programmes/:id/recognize`) and QR scanning (`/programmes/:id/scan-qr`) excluded via `NO_SYNC_PATTERNS` so they fail loudly instead of queueing ops that cannot be replayed; chat and users (`/users`)
136: 
137: #### Client-side data flow
138: - `request()` in `api.js` checks `navigator.onLine`:
139:   - **Online:** fetch from server; cache GET responses in `requestCache` for synced paths
140:   - **Offline:** GET reads from `requestCache`; POST/PUT/DELETE pushes to `pendingChanges` and returns optimistic result (`{ ...body, id: 'pending' }`)
141: - **Components show optimistic data immediately via `setAccounts` (local state)** — `handleCreate`, `handleUpdate`, `handleDelete` in `ParticipantManagement.jsx` skip the stale cache and directly update state when offline
142: - **Offline-disabled UIs:** CameraPage capture/confirm buttons disabled; ChatInput shows "unavailable" placeholder; face upload skipped in ParticipantManagement
143: 
144: #### Sync lifecycle
145: 1. **Queue:** offline writes accumulate in `pendingChanges` (IndexedDB, persists across sessions)
146: 2. **Trigger:** `useSync.js` fires `changeHandler()` on mount, `online` event, or tab `focus` (with ref guard to prevent concurrent runs)
147: 3. **Send:** `changeHandler()` does `POST /sync` with `{ ops, timestamp }`; on 200 OK, deletes `pendingChanges`; `useSync.js` then dispatches `sync:done`
148: 4. **Server processing:** `syncController.js` `HANDLERS` map dispatches each op by `method + path` pattern; auth ops include `validateToken()` checks
149: 5. **UI refresh:** components listen for `sync:done` via `window.addEventListener('sync:done', ...)` and `sync:done` event to re-fetch fresh data: `ParticipantManagement.jsx`, `ProgrammePage.jsx`, `directory.jsx`
150: 6. **Connectivity indicator:** `useConnectivity.js` polls `pendingChanges` every 3s **and** listens for `sync:done` to instantly update `pendingCount`; camera & chat disabled when offline
151: 
152: #### Automated tests
153: - **Client offline layer** (`npm run test:sync` in `src/client`): `tests/sync/client-offline.test.mjs` runs the real `api.js`/`syncEngine.js` in Node via a loader hook (`tests/sync/meta-loader.cjs`) that injects `import.meta.env` and resolves extensionless imports; Dexie backed by `fake-indexeddb`. Covers GET caching, offline cache reads, offline write queueing, never-queued endpoints (login, recognize, scan-qr), optimistic results, auth headers, and the `/sync` flush (success clears, failure retains).
154: - **Server replay** (`npm run test:sync` in `src/server`): `tests/server-replay.test.cjs` creates a throwaway `OpenGlimpse_test` database and exercises `handleSync` against the real Sequelize models. Covers every `HANDLERS` pattern (batch/single attendance, ready-to-depart, programme/route/delegate CRUD, auth account create/delete, face upload), staff-vs-participant permission rules, and unknown-path skipping.
155: 
156: ### 4.5 Hardware (for Demo & Production)
157: - Development: laptop webcam acceptable with printed QR codes and mock data
158: - Final demo: mobile phone (Android/iOS) for live facial recognition, camera-based QR scanning
159: - QR badges: printed QR codes embedded in delegate badge lanyard
160: - NFC badges: optional for future enhancement; requires NFC-equipped phone
161: 
162: ---
163: 
164: ## 5. Integration Points
165: 
166: - Ryan calls: `POST /programmes/{id}/scans` with facial embedding + confidence
167: - XY calls: `PUT /programmes/{id}/attendance/{delegateId}` for manual mark present/absent
168: - Ryan & XY listen: WebSocket event `attendance:updated` to refresh dashboard in real time
169: - Rayhan manages: offline queue — client-side buffers scan payloads, backend deduplicates on sync
170: - Matt ensures: JWT tokens issued by auth endpoint are validated by all API consumers
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: ## 6. Success Criteria
175: 
176: | Metric | Target |
177: |--------|--------|
178: | Time to reconcile 30 pax | < 1 minute |
179: | Time to reconcile 100+ pax | < 2 minutes |
180: | Facial recognition accuracy | ≥99% with staff confirmation for matches |
181: | Data loss on offline sync | Zero |
182: | Staff usability score | ≥4.5 / 5 |
183: | China accessibility | Fully functional on Alibaba Cloud; no GFW blocks |
184: | Cloud sync latency | < 2 seconds for multi-device updates |
185: 
186: ---
187: 
188: ## 7. Out of Scope
189: 
190: - Real-time location tracking or GPS maps (client uses WhatsApp)
191: - Liveness detection / anti-spoofing (client prioritises speed over security compliance)
192: - Government compliance audit trails
193: - Integration with external HR, CRM, or event management systems
194: - Push notifications beyond in-app alerts
195: - Voice calls or video conferencing (WhatsApp remains communication channel)
196: 
197: ---
198: 
199: ## 8. Assumptions & Risks
200: 
201: ### 8.1 Assumptions
202: - Internet (cellular data or hotspot) is available at all trip locations (China, ASEAN countries)
203: - Client will provide sample participant data: names + passport-sized facial photos
204: - Staff members have smartphones capable of running React web app (Android/iOS, modern browsers)
205: - Face-api.js embeddings are sufficient for matching with ≥99% accuracy among diverse delegate faces
206: - PostgreSQL with pgvector extension (or JSONB) is available on hosting provider
207: 
208: ### 8.2 Risks & Mitigation
209: 
210: | Risk | Mitigation |
211: |------|------------|
212: | Facial recognition accuracy on diverse faces, varied lighting, or poor photo quality | Set clear confidence thresholds (0.6+); always offer manual override; test with diverse delegation photos early |
213: | Great Firewall blocks Alibaba Cloud or host provider | Verify Alibaba Cloud Singapore/HK region connectivity from China SIM in Week 1; have AWS HK as backup |
214: | Face-api.js embedding format incompatible with backend matching algorithm | Agree on embedding format (size, normalization) in Week 1; test sample embeddings on both sides |
215: | WebSocket scaling — many concurrent staff devices cause latency | Load test early; consider Socket.io room/namespace for per-programme isolation |
216: | Offline queue duplication — same scan synced twice on reconnect | Add unique scan ID (timestamp + device ID) to each offline queue item; backend deduplicates on ID |
217: | QR code as backup underutilised if FR works well | Defer QR printing to P2; clients may choose not to use if FR is reliable |
218: 
219: ---
220: 
221: ## 9. Individual Documentation
222: 
223: Per-team-member deep-dive docs (use cases, API reference, database schema) live under `docs/<student-name>/`, with the overall system architecture in `docs/architecture.md`:
224: 
225: - `docs/architecture.md` — system architecture overview
226: - `docs/ryan/use-cases.md` — use cases for all roles (facial recognition, QR backup, unidentified alerts, chatbot)
227: - `docs/ryan/api-documentation.md` — every HTTP endpoint + WebSocket/chat events + internal FaceNet API
228: - `docs/ryan/database-schema.md` — ER diagram + full table definitions for the PostgreSQL schema
229: 
230: ---
231: 
232: ## 10. Pages (UI)
233: 
234: - **Dashboard / Overview** — instant snapshot of delegate status; real-time counter (present/overall)
235: - **Scanner** — QR/NFC and facial scanning
236: - **Profile Page** — CRUD operations for delegate profiles
237: - **Support Tickets** — CRUD operations
238: - **Directory** — all delegates' name and info; manual check-in; notes (badge missing, verified manually)
239: - **Missing List** — shows who is missing; call button for direct contact; toggle for special occasions
240: - **Sync Log** — connectivity indicator (offline/online/syncing); pending sync count

(End of file - total 240 lines)
</content>

The approach: Rather than editing ~25 files and 490 usages with `dark:` variants, the cleanest, most reliable path for a Tailwind v4 project is to use CSS variables and `dark:` variants. But that would require adding `dark:` classes everywhere.

Actually, there's a much smarter approach for Tailwind v4: redefining the color palette variables at `@theme` level won't change because we still use `bg-white` etc.

The most pragmatic, robust approach to force a dark UI everywhere without touching all files: **override the color usage via CSS**. But editing inline utility classes is simpler... but 490 locations is a lot.

However, there's a very elegant trick: In Tailwind v4, colors are CSS variables referenced e.g. `.bg-white { background-color: var(--color-white); }`. But the actual stylesheet emits `background-color: var(--color-white)`. We could override the variables under a `.dark` scope... but bg-white inside sidebar in CSS var would change too — including `text-white` on colored buttons? No — `text-white` would become dark text, that's bad.

Better approach: do it properly with Tailwind class-based `dark:` variants. Enable `@custom-variant dark` in Tailwind v4 and add the `dark` class to the root. Then add `dark:` classes to every element. But that's 490 edits across 25 files — very large but doable via careful batch editing.

Given the scale, the most efficient and safe approach is to define the dark overrides **in the CSS** scoped under `.dark` using the existing utility classes, since specificity: `.dark .bg-white` (0,2,0) beats `.bg-white` (0,1,0). useTheme.js:
```js
import { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from 'react';

const STORAGE_KEY = 'theme';

function getInitial() {
  const stored = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
  if (stored === 'light' || stored === 'dark') return stored;
  return 'dark';
}

export function useTheme() {
  const [theme, setTheme] = useState(getInitialTheme);

  useEffect(() => {
    document.documentElement.classList.toggle('dark', theme === 'dark');
    localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, theme);
  }, [theme]);

  const toggleTheme = useCallback(() => {
    setTheme((t) => (t === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark'));
  }, []);

  return { theme, toggleTheme };
}
```

2: const { parseToken } = require('../auth/authRoutes');

8: function formatpayload(row, senderRole, reactions = [], senderName = null) {
9:     return {
10:         id: row.id,
11:         text: row.content ?? row.text,
12:         timestamp: row.timestamp,
13:         senderId: row.senderId,
14:         senderRole: senderRole || null,
15:         senderName: senderName || null,
16:         reactions,

18: }

20: async function reactionsForMessages(messageIds) {
21:     if (messageIds.length === 0) return {};
22:     const rows = await Reactions.readByMessageIds(messageIds);
23:     const byMessage = {};
24:     for (const row of rows) {
25:         const mid = row.messageId;
26:         if (!byMessage[mid]) byMessage[mid] = {};
27:         if (!byMessage[mid][row.emoji]) byMessage[mid][row.emoji] = [];
28:         byMessage[mid][row.emoji].push(row.userId);
29:     }
30:     const out = {};
31:     for (const mid of Object.keys(byMessage)) {
32:         out[mid] = Object.entries(byMessage[mid])
33:             .map(([emoji, userIds]) => ({ emoji, userIds }))
34:             .sort((a, b) => b.userIds.length - a.userIds.length);
35:     }
36:     return out;
37: }

39: function attachChatServer(io, getChatbotUserId) {
40:     const chat = io.of('/chat');
41: 
42:     chat.use(async (socket, next) => {
43:         try {
44:             const token = socket.handshake.auth?.token || socket.handshake.query?.token;
45:             if (!token) {
46:                 return next(new Error('Authentication required'));
47:             }
48: 
49:             const payload = parseToken(token);
50:             if (!payload?.id) {
51:                 return next(new Error('Invalid token'));
52:             }
53: 
54:             const currentUser = await user.findByPk(payload.id);
55:             if (!currentUser) {
56:                 return next(new Error('Invalid user'));
57:             }
58: 
59:             socket.userId = currentUser.id;
60:             socket.userRole = currentUser.role;
61:             socket.userName = currentUser.enName;
62:             next();
63:         } catch (err) {
64:             next(new Error('Authentication failed'));
65:         }
66:     });
67: 
68:     chat.on('connection', (socket) => {
69:         console.log(`Chat user connected: ${socket.userId}`);
70: 
71:         socket.programmeId = null;
72: 
73:         const chatbotUserId = getChatbotUserId();
74:         if (chatbotUserId) {
75:             socket.emit('chatbot:config', { userId: chatbotUserId, trigger: CHATBOT_TRIGGER });
76:         }
77: 
78:         socket.on('chat:join', (programmeId) => {
79:             socket.programmeId = programmeId;
80:         });
81: 
82:         (async () => {
83:             const history = await Messages.read();
84:             const senderIds = [...new Set(history.map((m) => m.senderId))];
85:             const senders = await user.findAll({ where: { id: senderIds }, attributes: ['id', 'role', 'enName'] });
86:             const roleById = Object.fromEntries(senders.map((u) => [u.id, u.role]));
87:             const nameById = Object.fromEntries(senders.map((u) => [u.id, u.enName]));
88:             const reactions = await reactionsForMessages(history.map((m) => m.id));
89:             socket.emit('history', {
90:                 messages: history.map((m) => formatpayload(m, roleById[m.senderId], reactions[m.id] || [], nameById[m.senderId] || null)),
91:             });
92:         })().catch((err) => {
93:             console.error('Chat history could not be loaded', err);
94:             socket.emit('error', { text: 'Chat history could not be found' });
95:         });
96: 
97:         socket.on('message', async (data) => {
98:             try {
99:                 const text = typeof data?.text === 'string' ? data.text.trim() : '';
100: 
101:                 if (!text || text.length > 1000) {
102:                     return socket.emit('error', { text: 'invalid message' });
103:                 }
104: 
105:                 const savedMessage = await Messages.create({
106:                     content: text,
107:                     timestamp: new Date(),
108:                     senderId: socket.userId,
109:                 });
110: 
111:                 chat.emit('message', {
112:                     message: formatpayload(savedMessage.toJSON(), socket.userRole, [], socket.userName),
113:                 });
114: 
115:                 if (text.startsWith(CHATBOT_TRIGGER) && socket.programmeId) {
116:                     const chatbotUserId = getChatbotUserId();
117:                     if (!chatbotUserId) return;
118: 
119:                     const userQuery = text.slice(CHATBOT_TRIGGER.length).trim();
120:                     if (!userQuery) return;
121: 
122:                     chat.emit('chatbot:typing', { senderId: chatbotUserId });
123: 
124:                     try {
125:                         const context = await buildProgrammeContext(socket.programmeId);
126:                         if (!context) {
127:                             chat.emit('chatbot:stop', { senderId: chatbotUserId });
128:                             return;
129:                         }
130: 
131:                         const reply = await getChatbotResponse(userQuery, context, chatbotUserId, socket.userId);
132: 
133:                         const botMessage = await Messages.create({
134:                             content: reply,
135:                             timestamp: new Date(),
136:                             senderId: chatbotUserId,
137:                         });
138: 
139:                         chat.emit('chatbot:stop', { senderId: chatbotUserId });
140:                         chat.emit('message', {
141:                             message: formatpayload(botMessage.toJSON()),
142:                         });
143:                     } catch (err) {

394: ProgrammeDelegate.addDelegates = async function (programmeId, body) {
395:   const { delegates, delegateIds, delegateId, name, badge, routeId, userIds } = body;
396:   const addToRoute = async (did) => {
397:     if (routeId) {
398:       // One route per delegate: move, don't duplicate
399:       await RouteMember.destroy({ where: { programmeId, delegateId: did } });
400:       await RouteMember.findOrCreate({ where: { routeId, delegateId: did, programmeId }, defaults: { routeId, delegateId: did, programmeId } });
401:     }
402:   };
403:   // New: accept userIds — find-or-create delegates by userId
404:   if (userIds && Array.isArray(userIds)) {
405:     const added = [];
406:     for (const uid of userIds) {
407:       let del = await Delegate.findOne({ where: { userId: uid } });
408:       if (!del) {
409:         const u = await user.findByPk(uid);
410:         if (!u) continue;
411:         del = await Delegate.create({ name: u.enName, userId: uid });
412:       }
413:       await ProgrammeDelegate.findOrCreate({ where: { programmeId, delegateId: del.id }, defaults: { programmeId, delegateId: del.id } });
414:       await addToRoute(del.id);
415:       added.push({ delegateId: del.id, name: del.name });
416:     }
417:     return added;
418:   }
419:   if (delegates && Array.isArray(delegates)) {
420:     const added = [];
421:     for (const d of delegates) {
422:       const [del] = await Delegate.findOrCreate({ where: { name: d.name }, defaults: { name: d.name, badge: d.badge || null } });
423:       await ProgrammeDelegate.findOrCreate({ where: { programmeId, delegateId: del.id }, defaults: { programmeId, delegateId: del.id } });
424:       await addToRoute(del.id);
425:       added.push({ delegateId: del.id, name: del.name });
426:     }
427:     return added;
428:   }
429:   if (delegateIds && Array.isArray(delegateIds)) {
430:     for (const id of delegateIds) {
431:       await ProgrammeDelegate.findOrCreate({ where: { programmeId, delegateId: id }, defaults: { programmeId, delegateId: id } });
432:       await addToRoute(id);
433:     }
434:     return delegateIds.map((id) => ({ delegateId: id }));
435:   }
436:   if (delegateId) {
437:     await ProgrammeDelegate.findOrCreate({ where: { programmeId, delegateId }, defaults: { programmeId, delegateId } });
438:     await addToRoute(delegateId);
439:     return [{ delegateId }];
440:   }
441:   if (name) {
442:     const del = await Delegate.create({ name, badge: badge || null });
443:     await ProgrammeDelegate.create({ programmeId, delegateId: del.id });
444:     await addToRoute(del.id);
445:     return [{ delegateId: del.id, name }];
446:   }
447:   throw new Error("Provide delegates array, delegateIds, delegateId, or name");
448: };

456: AttendanceRecord.getAttendance = async function (programmeId) {
457:   const presentRecords = await AttendanceRecord.findAll({ where: { programmeId, status: "present" }, order: [["checked_in_at", "DESC"]] });
458:   const presentDelegateIds = presentRecords.map((r) => r.delegateId);
459:   const allPds = await ProgrammeDelegate.findAll({
460:     where: { programmeId },
461:     attributes: {
462:       include: [
463:         [sequelize.literal(`(
464:           SELECT COALESCE(json_agg(json_build_object('id', rm.route_id, 'name', r.name) ORDER BY r.name), '[]'::json)
465:           FROM route_members rm
466:           JOIN routes r ON r.id = rm.route_id
467:           WHERE rm.delegate_id = "ProgrammeDelegate"."delegate_id" AND rm.programme_id = "ProgrammeDelegate"."programme_id"
468:         )`), "routes_json"],
469:       ],
470:     },
471:     include: [
472:       { model: Delegate, as: "delegate", attributes: ["id", "name"], required: true },
473:     ],
474:   });
475:   const pdByDelegateId = {};
476:   for (const pd of allPds) pdByDelegateId[pd.delegateId] = pd;
477:   const present = presentRecords.filter((rec) => pdByDelegateId[rec.delegateId]).map((rec) => {
478:     const pd = pdByDelegateId[rec.delegateId];
479:     const routes = pd.get("routes_json") || [];
480:     return {
481:       delegateId: rec.delegateId, name: pd.delegate.name,
482:       routeId: routes.length > 0 ? routes[0].id : null, routeName: routes.length > 0 ? routes[0].name : null,
483:       routeIds: routes.map((rt) => rt.id), routeNames: routes.map((rt) => rt.name),
484:       method: rec.method, checkedInAt: rec.checkedInAt, notes: rec.notes,
485:     };
486:   });
487:   const presentSet = new Set(presentDelegateIds);
488:   const missing = allPds.filter((pd) => !presentSet.has(pd.delegateId)).map((pd) => {
489:     const routes = pd.get("routes_json") || [];
490:     return {
491:       delegateId: pd.delegate.id, name: pd.delegate.name,
492:       routeId: routes.length > 0 ? routes[0].id : null, routeName: routes.length > 0 ? routes[0].name : null,
493:       routeIds: routes.map((rt) => rt.id), routeNames: routes.map((rt) => rt.name),
494:       notes: pd.notes || "",
495:     };
496:   });
497:   const unidentifiedEvents = await ScanEvent.findAll({ where: { programmeId, status: "unverified" }, attributes: ["id", "scannedAt"], order: [["scanned_at", "DESC"]] });
498:   return { present, missing, unidentified: unidentifiedEvents.map((s) => ({ scanId: s.id, scannedAt: s.scannedAt })) };
499: };
500: AttendanceRecord.markAttendance = async function (programmeId, delegateId, { status, method, notes }, io) {
501:   if (!["present", "absent"].includes(status)) throw new Error('status must be "present" or "absent"');
502:   if (status === "present" && !method) throw new Error("method is required when marking present");
503:   if (!(await ProgrammeDelegate.findOne({ where: { programmeId, delegateId } }))) throw new Error("Delegate is not in this programme");
504:   const existing = await AttendanceRecord.findOne({ where: { programmeId, delegateId } });
505:   let row;
506:   if (existing) {
507:     await existing.update({ status, method: method || "manual", notes: notes || "", checkedInAt: new Date() });
508:     row = existing;
509:   } else {
510:     row = await AttendanceRecord.create({ programmeId, delegateId, status, method: method || "manual", notes: notes || "", checkedInAt: new Date() });
511:   }
512:   if (status === "present") {
513:     await ScanEvent.destroy({ where: { programmeId, delegateId: null, status: "unverified" } });
514:   }

17: ### 2.1 Primary Use Case
18: **Title:** Real-Time Facial Recognition Attendance with Multi-Staff Sync
19: 
20: **Goal:** Allow SCCCI secretariat staff to take attendance for an overseas delegation in under 1 minute (30 pax) or 2 minutes (100+ pax) using facial recognition, with instant visibility of who is present or absent — across multiple staff devices simultaneously.
21: 
22: **Actors:**

27: ### 2.2 Preconditions

34: ### 2.3 Main Flow (Happy Path)

39: 5. App matches detected face against stored delegate embeddings. If match confidence is high, delegate is marked Present automatically.
40: 6. If confidence is low or face is unrecognised, admin receives in-app alert. Staff can manually confirm identity from the list or use QR code backup.
41: 7. Attendance record syncs instantly to the cloud. All staff devices update in real time.
42: 8. The dashboard shows: Present list (with photos), Unidentified/Absent list (highlighted at top), and Ready-to-Depart status.
43: 9. When all delegates are accounted for, the Trip Manager confirms departure readiness.

45: ### 2.4 Alternative & Exception Flows

127: ### 4.4 Offline Sync Engine
128: 
129: #### Architecture
130: - **Client:** Dexie.js (IndexedDB) with `requestCache` and `pendingChanges` tables
131: - **Interception layer:** `services/api.js` `request()` caches GET responses; offline reads serve from cache, offline writes queue `{ method, path, body, token }` to `pendingChanges`
132: - **Auth endpoints:** `/api/auth` and `/api/user` in `SYNC_PREFIXES`; login excluded via `NEVER_QUEUE`; token carried in ops for auth writes
133: - **Sync trigger:** `hooks/useSync.js` calls `sync/changeHandler()` on mount, `online` event, and tab `focus`; dispatches `sync:start` before flushing and `sync:done` after (in `finally`, so it also fires on failure) to drive the syncing indicator and `pendingCount` refresh
134: - **Server:** `POST /sync` registered in `index.js` via `registerSyncRoutes(app)`; handled by `modules/sync/syncController.js` which replays ops against Sequelize models; auth ops validated via `parseToken()` + DB lookup
135: - **Vite proxy:** `/sync` added to `vite.config.js` proxy table so `changeHandler` fetch reaches Express (was root cause of silent sync failure)
136: - **Synced entity types:** programme, route, delegate, attendance (single + batch), readyToDepart, auth, face upload (`PATCH /api/user/:id/face/default`); batch attendance pulls `programmeId` from the URL path since the client payload only carries `records`
137: - **Not synced:** login (`/api/auth/login`); face recognition (`/programmes/:id/recognize`) and QR scanning (`/programmes/:id/scan-qr`) excluded via `NO_SYNC_PATTERNS` so they fail loudly instead of queueing ops that cannot be replayed; chat and users (`/users`)
138: 
139: #### Client-side data flow
140: - `request()` in `api.js` checks `navigator.onLine`:
141:   - **Online:** fetch from server; cache GET responses in `requestCache` for synced paths
142:   - **Offline:** GET reads from `requestCache`; POST/PUT/DELETE pushes to `pendingChanges` and returns optimistic result (`{ ...body, id: 'pending' }`)
143: - **Components show optimistic data immediately via `setAccounts` (local state)** — `handleCreate`, `handleUpdate`, `handleDelete` in `ParticipantManagement.jsx` skip the stale cache and directly update state when offline
144: - **Offline-disabled UIs:** CameraPage capture/confirm buttons disabled; ChatInput shows "unavailable" placeholder; face upload skipped in ParticipantManagement
145: 
146: #### Sync lifecycle
147: 1. **Queue:** offline writes accumulate in `pendingChanges` (IndexedDB, persists across sessions)
148: 2. **Trigger:** `useSync.js` fires `changeHandler()` on mount, `online` event, or tab `focus` (with ref guard to prevent concurrent runs)
149: 3. **Send:** `changeHandler()` does `POST /sync` with `{ ops, timestamp }`; on 200 OK, deletes `pendingChanges`; `useSync.js` then dispatches `sync:done`
150: 4. **Server processing:** `syncController.js` `HANDLERS` map dispatches each op by `method + path` pattern; auth ops include `validateToken()` checks
151: 5. **UI refresh:** components listen for `sync:done` via `window.addEventListener('sync:done', ...)` and `sync:done` event to re-fetch fresh data: `ParticipantManagement.jsx`, `ProgrammePage.jsx`, `directory.jsx`
152: 6. **Connectivity indicator:** `useConnectivity.js` polls `pendingChanges` every 3s **and** listens for `sync:done` to instantly update `pendingCount`; camera & chat disabled when offline
153: 
154: #### Automated tests
155: - **Client offline layer** (`npm run test:sync` in `src/client`): `tests/sync/client-offline.test.mjs` runs the real `api.js`/`syncEngine.js` in Node via a loader hook (`tests/sync/meta-loader.cjs`) that injects `import.meta.env` and resolves extensionless imports; Dexie backed by `fake-indexeddb`. Covers GET caching, offline cache reads, offline write queueing, never-queued endpoints (login, recognize, scan-qr), optimistic results, auth headers, and the `/sync` flush (success clears, failure retains).

Covers every `HANDLERS` pattern (batch/single attendance, ready-to-depart, programme/route/delegate CRUD, auth account create/delete, face upload), staff-vs-participant permission rules, and unknown-path skipping.

#### Overview
In-app chat built on a dedicated Socket.io namespace `/chat`, separate from the attendance socket in `services/socket.js`.   - `message` (client → server): validates text (non-empty, ≤1000 chars), persists via `Messages.create`, broadcasts `message` to the whole `/chat` namespace. If text starts with the chatbot trigger (e.g. `@assistant`) and a programme is joined, emits `chatbot:typing`, builds programme context, calls Groq, persists the bot reply, then emits `chatbot:stop` + `message`.

### 4.5 Real-Time Chat Feature

#### Overview
An in-app, programme-scoped chat with message persistence, emoji reactions, admin/highlighted bubbles, sender avatars, and an optional AI assistant. Built entirely by **Rayablepy** (Rayhan) on the `messages-update` / `feature/chat-improvements` branches and merged via PR #7 and the `feature/offline-sync-v3` line. Uses a dedicated Socket.io namespace (`/chat`) served from `src/server/modules/chat/chatserver.cjs` (separate from the attendance socket namespace) and a `@assistant`-triggered Groq chatbot.

#### Server-side architecture
- **Namespace:** Socket.io `io.of('/chat')` mounted in `index.js` via `attachChatServer(io, getChatbotUserId)`.
- **Auth middleware:** every socket handshake must supply a JWT (`auth.token` or `query.token`); `parseToken()` + `user.findByPk()` validate it and attach `userId`, `userRole`, `userName` to the socket.
- **History:** on connection, loads the last 100 `Messages` ordered ascending, joins each message's sender role/name, and resolves reactions via `Reactions.readByMessageIds`; emits `history` with the full formatted payload.
- **Events (client → server):**
  - `chat:join <programmeId>` — stores `socket.programmeId` for chatbot context.
  - `message { text }` — trims/validates (≤1000 chars), persists via `Messages.create`, broadcasts `message` to the whole `/chat` namespace; if the text starts with the chatbot trigger (e.g. `@assistant`) and a programme is joined, builds programme context and streams a Groq response (emitting `chatbot:typing` / `chatbot:stop` around it and persisting the bot reply).
  - `react { messageId, emoji }` — toggles a per-user reaction on a message (same emoji → delete; different emoji → update; else create), then broadcasts `reaction:update` with the aggregated `{ emoji, userIds[] }` list, sorted by count.
- **Chatbot config:** on connection the server emits `chatbot:config` (`{ userId, trigger }`) so the client knows how to render bot bubbles; the chatbot user is seeded as `ai-assistant@openglimpse.com` on startup (`index.js`).

#### Database models (`db.cjs` + `dbcrudmethods.js`)
- `messages` (`content`, `timestamp`, `senderId` → `users`) — chat message persistence, written by Rayable's original chat/db commits (`0ee92b6`) and extended with `senderId` (`7e96bda`).
- `message_reactions` (`messageId` → `messages`, `userId` → `users`, `emoji`; unique on `(message_id, user_id)`) — one reaction per user per message.
- CRUD classes: `Messages` (create/read last 100/update/delete) and `Reactions` (create/findOne/update/destroy/readByMessageIds) in `server/database/dbcrudmethods.js`.

#### Client-side components (`src/client/src/pages/chat/`)
- `chat.jsx` — main page: connects `io(`${VITE_CHAT_SERVER_URL}/chat`, { auth: { token }, transports: ['websocket'] })`, joins the selected programme, renders the message list, fetches programmes + staff for mentions, tracks scroll position with a jump-to-bottom button + unread count, and shows online/offline pills. Redirects to `/profile` when the device goes offline (`e0a85c8`), and disables the composer with a "Chat unavailable while offline" placeholder.
- `chatbubble.jsx` — message bubble; own/other alignment via `chat-bubble-own`/`chat-bubble-other`, admin bubbles highlighted with `chat-bubble-admin` (`9908dc8`), bot bubbles render Markdown via `marked` with a "BOT" badge, sender avatars (`e335d56`), and per-bubble emoji reactions triggered by hover or long-press (`chatbubble.jsx` + `ReactionBar.jsx`).
- `ChatInput.jsx` — textarea composer with `@` mention suggestions (staff names + `@assistant`), keyboard navigation (arrows/enter/tab/escape), and a gradient send button.
- `ReactionBar.jsx` — quick-emoji palette (👍 ❤️ 😂 😮 😢 🙏) shown above a bubble.

#### Chat UI styling (`index.css`)
`.chat-*` classes: layout (`chat-page`, `chat-header`, `chat-layout`, `chat-scroll`, `chat-content`, `chat-composer-shell`), bubbles (`chat-bubble-own`/`-other`/`-bot`/`-admin`, `chat-bubble-time-*`), reactions (`chat-reactions`, `chat-reaction`, `chat-reaction-mine`, `chat-reaction-bar`), mention dropdown, and the gradient `chat-send-button` / `chat-jump-bottom` (sky gradient via the combined selector).

#### Chatbot (`server/modules/chatbot/chatbot.js`)
- Groq API client; `buildProgrammeContext(programmeId)` assembles a text context from programme, routes, delegates, attendance summary, and staff list; `getChatbotResponse` injects a system prompt + recent 10-message history and calls the model (`GROQ_MODEL`, default `gpt-oss-20b`). Triggered only when the first word matches `VITE_CHATBOT_TRIGGER` (default `@assistant`).

#### Related env vars
- `VITE_CHAT_SERVER_URL` — Socket.io chat endpoint (client).
- `VITE_CHATBOT_TRIGGER` (default `@assistant`) and `GROQ_API_KEY` / `GROQ_MODEL` — chatbot trigger + provider config.

169:   - `chat:join <programmeId>` — stores `socket.programmeId` for chatbot context.
170:   - `message { text }` — trims/validates (≤1000 chars), persists via `Messages.create`, broadcasts `message` to the whole `/chat` namespace; if the text starts with the chatbot trigger (e.g. `@assistant`) and a programme is joined, builds programme context and streams a Groq response (emitting `chatbot:typing` / `chatbot:stop` around it and persisting the bot reply).
171:   - `react { messageId, emoji }` — toggles a per-user reaction on a message (same emoji → delete; different emoji → update; else create), then broadcasts `reaction:update` with the aggregated `{ emoji, userIds[] }` list, sorted by count.
172: - **Chatbot config:** on connection the server emits `chatbot:config` (`{ userId, trigger }`) so the client knows how to render bot bubbles; the chatbot user is seeded as `ai-assistant@openglimpse.com` on startup (`index.js`).
173: 
174: #### Database models (`db.cjs` + `dbcrudmethods.js`)
175: - `messages` (`content`, `timestamp`, `senderId` → `users`) — chat message persistence, written by Rayable's original chat/db commits (`0ee92b6`) and extended with `senderId` (`7e96bda`).
176: - `message_reactions` (`messageId` → `messages`, `userId` → `users`, `emoji`; unique on `(message_id, user_id)`) — one reaction per user per message.
177: - CRUD classes: `Messages` (create/read last 100/update/delete) and `Reactions` (create/findOne/update/destroy/readByMessageIds) in `server/database/dbcrudmethods.js`.
178: 
179: #### Client-side components (`src/client/src/pages/chat/`)
180: - `chat.jsx` — main page: connects `io(`${VITE_CHAT_SERVER_URL}/chat`, { auth: { token }, transports: ['websocket'] })`, joins the selected programme, renders the message list, fetches programmes + staff for mentions, tracks scroll position with a jump-to-bottom button + unread count, and shows online/offline pills. Redirects to `/profile` when the device goes offline (`e0a85c8`), and disables the composer with a "Chat unavailable while offline" placeholder.
181: - `chatbubble.jsx` — message bubble; own/other alignment via `chat-bubble-own`/`chat-bubble-other`, admin bubbles highlighted with `chat-bubble-admin` (`9908dc8`), bot bubbles render Markdown via `marked` with a "BOT" badge, sender avatars (`e335d56`), and per-bubble emoji reactions triggered by hover or long-press (`chatbubble.jsx` + `ReactionBar.jsx`).
182: - `ChatInput.jsx` — textarea composer with `@` mention suggestions (staff names + `@assistant`), keyboard navigation (arrows/enter/tab/escape), and a gradient send button.
183: - `ReactionBar.jsx` — quick-emoji palette (👍 ❤️ 😂 😮 😢 🙏) shown above a bubble.
184: 
185: #### Chat UI styling (`index.css`)
186: `.chat-*` classes: layout (`chat-page`, `chat-header`, `chat-layout`, `chat-scroll`, `chat-content`, `chat-composer-shell`), bubbles (`chat-bubble-own`/`-other`/`-bot`/`-admin`, `chat-bubble-time-*`), reactions (`chat-reactions`, `chat-reaction`, `chat-reaction-mine`, `chat-reaction-bar`), mention dropdown, and the gradient `chat-send-button` / `chat-jump-bottom` (sky gradient via the combined selector).
187: 
188: #### Chatbot (`server/modules/chatbot/chatbot.js`)
189: - Groq API client; `buildProgrammeContext(programmeId)` assembles a text context from programme, routes, delegates, attendance summary, and staff list; `getChatbotResponse` injects a system prompt + recent 10-message history and calls the model (`GROQ_MODEL`, default `gpt-oss-20b`). Triggered only when the first word matches `VITE_CHATBOT_TRIGGER` (default `@assistant`).
190: 
191: #### Related env vars
192: - `VITE_CHAT_SERVER_URL` — Socket.io chat endpoint (client).
193: - `VITE_CHATBOT_TRIGGER` (default `@assistant`) and `GROQ_API_KEY` / `GROQ_MODEL` — chatbot trigger + provider config.
194: 
195: ### 4.6 Hardware (for Demo & Production)
196: - Development: laptop webcam acceptable with printed QR codes and mock data
197: - Final demo: mobile phone (Android/iOS) for live facial recognition, camera-based QR scanning
198: - QR badges: printed QR codes embedded in delegate badge lanyard
199: - NFC badges: optional for future enhancement; requires NFC-equipped phone
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ## 5. Integration Points
204: 
205: - Ryan calls: `POST /programmes/{id}/scans` with facial embedding + confidence
206: - XY calls: `PUT /programmes/{id}/attendance/{delegateId}` for manual mark present/absent

1: # Use Cases — Ryan (Facial Recognition, QR Codes, Chatbot)
2: 
3: All user roles of OpenGlimpse: **Admin / Trip Manager (Staff)**, **Secretariat Staff (Staff)**, and **Delegate (Participant)**. Each use case names the actor, trigger, main flow, and edge-case / alternative flows.
4: 
5: **Scope:** These use cases cover Ryan's features only — face recognition, QR codes, and the chatbot. Flows reference supporting features owned by other members (auth/login, programme & delegate management, attendance, and offline `/sync`); those are documented by their respective owners.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## 1. Real-Time Facial Recognition Attendance
10: 
11: ### 1.1 UC-FR-01: Automatically Mark Delegate Present via Facial Recognition
12: 
13: - **Actor:** Secretariat Staff (primary), Delegate (secondary)
14: - **Trigger:** Delegate boards a coach or enters a venue while staff has the camera open on the attendance screen.
15: - **Main flow:**
16:   1. Staff opens the camera screen for the assigned programme/route.
17:   2. The app captures the video stream and detects faces in real time.
18:   3. A bounding box is drawn around every detected face in the camera view so staff can confirm all faces are being captured.
19:   4. The app submits each captured face image to `POST /programmes/:id/recognize`.
20:   5. Backend generates a FaceNet embedding for each face and compares (cosine similarity, threshold ≥ 0.5) against stored `primary` face embeddings in the `faceEmbeddings` table.
21:   6. For each match, a verified `ScanEvent` is created (programme module's `scan_events` table) and the delegate match is returned with confidence score.
22:   7. Staff confirms the match; `PUT /programmes/:id/attendance/:delegateId` is called with `status: present`, `method: auto` (attendance endpoint — programme module).
23:   8. All staff devices receive the `attendance:updated` WebSocket event and the dashboard updates in real time (socket broadcast — programme module).
24: - **Edge / alternative flows:**
25:   - *No face detected in image:* backend creates an `unverified` ScanEvent with reason "No face detected in image" and returns an empty `matches` array (no error thrown).
26:   - *No matching face found:* backend creates an `unverified` ScanEvent ("No matching face found"); admin receives the alert via dashboard `unidentified` list.
27:   - *Low confidence match:* staff manually confirms identity from the top-candidate list, or falls back to QR scan.
28:   - *Delegate not registered in this programme:* match is skipped server-side (`inProgramme` check).
29:   - *Multiple faces in frame:* each face is matched independently; multiple matches are returned sorted by descending confidence.
30:   - *Offline:* camera capture is disabled; queued offline scans are synced via `POST /sync` when connectivity returns (sync module).
31: 
32: ### 1.2 UC-FR-02: Register a Delegate's Face During Account Creation
33: 
34: - **Actor:** Admin / Trip Manager
35: - **Trigger:** A new user account (delegate or staff) is created and a facial photo needs to be stored.
36: - **Main flow:**
37:   1. Admin submits `POST /api/auth` with user details and an optional base64 `faceImage` (account creation — auth module).
38:   2. `FaceEmbeddings.createFromImage` sends the image to the Python FaceNet server (`/embed-all`).
39:   3. Each detected face crop is embedded and stored in `faceEmbeddings` with `imageType: 'primary'`.
40:   4. The photo is retrievable later via `GET /api/user/:id/face/default`.
41: - **Edge / alternative flows:**
42:   - *Face upload fails* (e.g., no face detected): failure is logged but account creation still succeeds.
43:   - *User uploads a new photo later:* `PATCH /api/user/:id/face/default` deletes all existing `primary` embeddings for the user and replaces them with the new image's embeddings.
44:   - *Multiple faces in the photo:* one embedding record is created per detected face.
45: 
46: ### 1.3 UC-FR-03: Verify Staff Identity on First Login
47: 
48: - **Actor:** Secretariat Staff
49: - **Trigger:** New staff member's first login after account creation.
50: - **Main flow:**
51:   1. Staff logs in via `POST /api/auth/login` (login — auth module).
52:   2. App compares the live face against the user's stored `primary` face embedding (`GET /api/user/:id/face/default`).
53:   3. On match, access is granted to staff screens.
54: - **Edge / alternative flows:**
55:   - *No face stored:* app prompts staff to upload a photo (`PATCH /api/user/:id/face/default`).
56:   - *Verification fails:* staff retries in better lighting; login itself is still credential-based, so staff can fall back to QR/manual attendance.
57: 
58: ---
59: 
60: ## 2. QR Code Backup Scanning
61: 
62: ### 2.1 UC-QR-01: Scan QR Badge to Mark Delegate Present
63: 
64: - **Actor:** Secretariat Staff (primary), Delegate (secondary)
65: - **Trigger:** Facial recognition fails or is unavailable; delegate presents the QR code from their badge (or from a tab on their phone).
66: - **Main flow:**
67:   1. Staff switches to the QR scanner tab in the app.
68:   2. The camera reads the QR code, which encodes the delegate's badge string.
69:   3. App calls `POST /programmes/:id/scan-qr` with the scanned `badge` value.
70:   4. Backend resolves the badge to a delegate in the programme and returns the delegate's id, name, and photo.
71:   5. Staff confirms and marks attendance via `PUT /programmes/:id/attendance/:delegateId` with `method: qr` (attendance endpoint — programme module).
72: - **Edge / alternative flows:**
73:   - *Badge not found:* the endpoint returns an error entry in the `errors` array; staff can manually mark the delegate present instead.
74:   - *Multiple badges scanned in one session:* the endpoint accepts a `badges` array for batch lookup.
75:   - *No badge assigned to delegate:* staff uses manual override; admin assigns a badge later via delegate profile.
76:   - *QR scan initiated offline:* QR endpoints are not synced; scanning requires connectivity.
77: 
78: ### 2.2 UC-QR-02: Manually Add a Person Not Captured by Face or QR
79: 
80: - **Actor:** Secretariat Staff / Admin
81: - **Trigger:** A person arrives whose face was not captured (poor photo, new late joiner) or whose QR was lost.
82: - **Main flow:**
83:   1. Staff taps "Add" from the delegate management screen.
84:   2. Staff enters the person's name (and optionally badge) via `POST /programmes/:id/delegates` (delegate management — programme module).
85:   3. The person appears in the programme delegate list and can be marked present manually.
86: - **Edge / alternative flows:**
87:   - *Late joiner has an existing user account:* add via `userIds` so the delegate links to the user and its face embeddings become matchable.
88:   - *Name already exists:* `findOrCreate` reuses the existing delegate row; programme membership is created idempotently.
89: 
90: ---
91: 
92: ## 3. Unidentified Face Alerting
93: 
94: ### 3.1 UC-AL-01: Alert Admins of Unidentified Faces
95: 
96: - **Actor:** Admin / Trip Manager (recipient), Secretariat Staff (source)
97: - **Trigger:** A captured face fails to match any registered programme delegate (confidence below threshold or no candidate).
98: - **Main flow:**
99:   1. `POST /programmes/:id/recognize` creates a `ScanEvent` with `status: 'unverified'` and a reason (scan event — programme module).
100:   2. Attendance summary (`GET /programmes/:id/attendance/summary`, programme module) counts unverified scans; dashboards list them with scan id and timestamp.
101:   3. Admins see the unidentified count in real time and investigate (compare to manual roster, ask staff to re-scan, or add the person manually).
102:   4. Once the person is identified and marked present, unresolved unverified scan events for the programme are cleared.
103: - **Edge / alternative flows:**
104:   - *False positive (verified delegate later re-scanned):* the cleared-unverified logic only removes unresolved events when a delegate is marked present.
105:   - *Person turns out to be non-delegate:* admin ignores the alert; events remain in the unidentified list for audit.
106: 
107: ---
108: 
109: ## 4. Chatbot Assistant
110: 
111: ### 4.1 UC-CH-01: Ask the Assistant About the Programme
112: 
113: - **Actor:** Any staff member
114: - **Trigger:** A message starting with the configured trigger prefix (default `@assistant`) is sent in the programme chat.
115: - **Main flow:**
116:   1. Staff sends `@assistant <question>` in the chat namespace (chat module).
117:   2. The message is stored (`chat_messages`, chat module), broadcast to all chat users, then routed to the chatbot.
118:   3. `chatbot:typing` is emitted; the backend builds a full programme context (delegates, routes, attendance summary, staff list) via `buildProgrammeContext` (programme module data).
119:   4. The Groq API (model from `GROQ_MODEL`, default `gpt-oss-20b`) receives system prompt + last 10 messages + the user query.
120:   5. The reply is stored as a message from the seeded AI Assistant user (`ai-assistant@openglimpse.com`) and broadcast; `chatbot:stop` is emitted.
121: - **Edge / alternative flows:**
122:   - *Message too long (> 1000 chars) or empty:* server emits an `error` event, message rejected.
123:   - *User not joined to a programme (`chat:join` not sent):* chatbot is not invoked; message is still saved and broadcast.
124:   - *No chatbot user seeded:* chatbot responses are silently skipped.
125:   - *Groq API failure / no programme context:* `chatbot:stop` emitted and an `error` event with "Chatbot could not respond" is sent to the socket.
126:   - *Question unrelated to programme:* the bot answers helpfully but notes it has programme-specific knowledge.
127:

1: # API Documentation — OpenGlimpse Express Backend (Ryan)
2: 
3: Base URL: `http://<host>:3001` (dev default port 3001; frontend proxies `/` to this server via Vite).
4: 
5: - All JSON. Request body limit: 10 MB.
6: - Response envelope errors: `404 Not Found` → `{ "error": "..." }`, `500` → `{ "error": "...", "detail": "..." }` (unhandled error handler) or just `{ "error": "..." }`.
7: 
8: **Scope:** This document covers Ryan's features only — face recognition, QR badge lookup, and the chatbot. These features depend on other members' work:
9: 
10: - **Auth (`/api/auth`)** — accounts, login, and the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` mechanism (auth module).
11: - **Programmes, routes, delegates, attendance** — `/programmes/:id` scoping, delegate membership, and attendance recording (programme module).
12: - **`/sync`** — offline replay (sync module).
13: 
14: Those endpoints and tables are documented by the respective module owners.
15: 
16: **Error code reference used across the API:**
17: 
18: | Code | Meaning |
19: |------|---------|
20: | 400 | Bad request (missing/invalid fields, validation failure) |
21: | 404 | Resource not found |
22: | 500 | Internal server error |
23: 
24: ---
25: 
26: ## 1. Face Recognition
27: 
28: ### POST `/programmes/:id/recognize` — Match faces in a live capture
29: 
30: - **Auth:** `Bearer <token>` (auth module)
31: - **Body:**
32:   ```json
33:   { "image": "base64-encoded-jpeg" }
34:   ```
35: - **Success (200):**
36:   ```json
37:   { "matches": [ { "delegateId": "uuid", "name": "Ah Ming", "confidence": 0.82, "imageData": "base64" } ] }
38:   ```
39:   Empty `matches: []` when no face detected or no match (an `unverified` `ScanEvent` is recorded in both cases).
40: - **Errors:** 400 (image required; invalid programme UUID), 500
41: - **Threshold:** cosine similarity ≥ 0.5 against `faceEmbeddings` rows with `imageType: 'primary'`; only matches delegates already in the programme (delegate membership provided by the programme module). Matches are sorted by descending confidence.
42: 
43: ### POST `/api/user/:id/face` — Register face cache image for a user
44: 
45: - **Auth:** `Bearer <token>` (auth module)
46: - **Body:** `{ "image": "base64" }`
47: - **Success (201):** `[ { "imageHash": "sha256", "embeddings": "[...floats...]", "model": "facenet" } ]`
48: - **Errors:** 400 (missing image), 404 (user not found), 500
49: 
50: ### PATCH `/api/user/:id/face/default` — Set/overwrite primary face
51: 
52: - **Auth:** `Bearer <token>` (auth module)
53: - **Body:** `{ "image": "base64" }`
54: - **Behavior:** deletes all existing `primary` embeddings for the user, then embeds the new image.
55: - **Success (200):** `[ { "hash", "embedding", "model" } ]`
56: - **Errors:** 400, 404, 500
57: 
58: ### GET `/api/user/:id/face/default` — Get primary face embeddings
59: 
60: - **Auth:** `Bearer <token>` (auth module)
61: - **Success (200):** `[ { "hash", "imageData": "base64", "embedding": "[floats]", "model": "facenet" } ]`
62: - **Errors:** 404 (no default face / user not found), 500
63: 
64: ---
65: 
66: ## 2. QR Badge Lookup
67: 
68: ### POST `/programmes/:id/scan-qr` — Resolve badge(s) to delegates
69: 
70: - **Auth:** `Bearer <token>` (auth module)
71: - **Body:** `{ "badge": "A001" }` **or** `{ "badges": ["A001", "A002"] }`
72: - **Success (200):**
73:   ```json
74:   { "matches": [ { "delegateId": "uuid", "name": "Ah Ming", "badge": "A001", "photoUrl": null } ],
75:     "errors": [ "no delegate found for badge: 999" ] }
76:   ```
77: - **Errors:** 400 (neither badge nor badges; badge empty), 500
78: - **Dependency:** delegate lookup and programme membership are provided by the programme module.
79: 
80: ---
81: 
82: ## 3. WebSocket — `/chat` namespace (Chatbot)
83: 
84: ### `/chat` namespace (auth: token via `handshake.auth.token` or `handshake.query.token`; token issued by auth module)
85: - Server → socket on connect: `chatbot:config { userId, trigger }`
86: - Client → server: `chat:join (programmeId)`, `message ({ text ≤ 1000 chars })`
87: - Server → all: `message ({ message: { id, content, timestamp, senderId } })`, `chatbot:typing { senderId }`, `chatbot:stop { senderId }`, `error ({ text })`
88: - On connection, server pushes `history { messages[] }` (last 100, ascending).
89: 
90: ---
91: 
92: ## 4. Misc
93: 
94: ### GET `/` — Health check

1: # Database Schema — OpenGlimpse (PostgreSQL + Sequelize) — Ryan
2: 
3: All definitions from `src/server/database/db.cjs` (models auto-synced with `sequelize.sync({ alter: true })`). All UUID PKs default to `uuidv4`. Column names shown are the actual PostgreSQL column names (`field` mappings applied).
4: 
5: **Scope:** This document covers the tables owned by Ryan's features only — face recognition, QR badge lookup, and the chatbot. The following tables are owned by other members and depend on their modules (documented by the respective owners):
6: 
7: - `programmes`, `routes`, `delegates`, `programme_delegates`, `attendance_records`, `route_members`, `ready_to_depart`, `scan_events` — programme/attendance module (Matthias)
8: - `messages`, `chat_messages` — chat module (Matthias)
9: - `offline_queue` — sync module
10: - `attendee`, `admin`, `staff` — legacy/unused
11: 
12: ---
13: 
14: ## 1. Entity-Relationship Diagram (Mermaid)
15: 
16: ```mermaid
17: erDiagram
18:     users ||--o{ faceEmbeddings : "owns (userId)"
19: ```
20: 
21: ---
22: 
23: ## 2. Table Definitions
24: 
25: ### 2.1 `users` — User accounts (staff & participants)
26: 
27: | Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
28: |--------|------|-------------|-------|
29: | `id` | UUID | **PK** | default uuidv4 |
30: | `enName` | STRING | NOT NULL | English name |
31: | `zhName` | STRING | NULL | Chinese name |
32: | `email` | TEXT | NOT NULL, **UNIQUE** | normalized lowercase |
33: | `password_hash` | TEXT | NULL | SHA-256 hex |
34: | `photo_url` | TEXT | NULL | |
35: | `role` | TEXT | `staff` \| `participant` | |
36: | `created_at` | DATE | | timestamps: created only |
37: 
38: **Relationships:** 1—N `faceEmbeddings.userId`. Other links (`messages.senderId`, `delegates.user_id`, `chat_messages.sender_id`) belong to other modules' tables.
39: 
40: ### 2.2 `faceEmbeddings` — Stored facial embeddings
41: 
42: | Column | Type | Constraints | Notes |
43: |--------|------|-------------|-------|
44: | `imageHash` | STRING | **PK** | SHA-256 of face crop |
45: | `userId` | UUID | NOT NULL, **FK → users.id** | |
46: | `imageType` | STRING | NOT NULL | `primary` (matching) \| `cache` |
47: | `imageData` | BLOB(long) | NOT NULL | JPEG bytes of face crop |
48: | `embeddings` | TEXT | NOT NULL | JSON array of floats (FaceNet, 512-dim) |
49: | `model` | STRING | NOT NULL | `facenet` |
50: 
51: **Note:** recognition (`POST /programmes/:id/recognize`) only matches against `imageType = 'primary'` rows; `PATCH /api/user/:id/face/default` replaces all primary embeddings for a user. Recognized delegates and scan results are stored in the programme module's `delegates` and `scan_events` tables.
52: 
53: ---
54: 
55: ## 3. Key Design Notes
56: 
57: - **Embedding storage:** FaceNet embeddings stored as JSON text in `faceEmbeddings.embeddings`; matching is done in Node (cosine similarity ≥ 0.5) rather than pgvector.
58: - **Dependencies:** Face recognition and QR lookup rely on the programme module's `delegates` / `programme_delegates` / `scan_events`; the chatbot relies on the chat module's `chat_messages`; auth relies on `users`.

(End of file - total 58 lines)
</content>

1: # Use Cases — Matthias (Login & Participant Creation)
2: 
3: Roles relevant here: **Admin / Trip Manager (Staff)**, **Secretariat Staff (Staff)**, and **Delegate (Participant)**. Each use case names the actor, trigger, main flow, and edge-case / alternative flows.
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## 1. Participant Creation
8: 
9: ### 1.1 UC-FR-02: Register a Delegate's Face During Account Creation
10: 
11: - **Actor:** Admin / Trip Manager
12: - **Trigger:** A new user account (delegate or staff) is created and a facial photo needs to be stored.
13: - **Main flow:**
14:   1. Admin submits `POST /api/auth` with user details and an optional base64 `faceImage`.
15:   2. `FaceEmbeddings.createFromImage` sends the image to the Python FaceNet server (`/embed-all`).
16:   3. Each detected face crop is embedded and stored in `faceEmbeddings` with `imageType: 'primary'`.
17:   4. The photo is retrievable later via `GET /api/user/:id/face/default`.
18: - **Edge / alternative flows:**
19:   - *Face upload fails* (e.g., no face detected): failure is logged but account creation still succeeds.
20:   - *User uploads a new photo later:* `PATCH /api/user/:id/face/default` deletes all existing `primary` embeddings for the user and replaces them with the new image's embeddings.
21:   - *Multiple faces in the photo:* one embedding record is created per detected face.
22: 
23: ---
24: 
25: ## 2. Login
26: 
27: ### 2.1 UC-FR-03: Verify Identity on First Login
28: 
29: - **Actor:** User (staff or participant)
30: - **Trigger:** New person's first login after account creation.
31: - **Main flow:**
32:   1. Person logs in via `POST /api/auth/login`.
33:   2. (Optional) App compares the live face against the stored `primary` face embedding (`GET /api/user/:id/face/default`).
34:   3. On match, access is granted.
35: - **Edge / alternative flows:**
36:   - *No face stored:* app prompts the person to upload a photo (`PATCH /api/user/:id/face/default`).
37:   - *Verification fails:* person retries in better lighting; login itself is still credential-based.
38: 
39: ### 2.2 UC-SUP-01: Login
40: 
41: - **Actor:** Staff / Admin / Participant
42: - **Trigger:** User opens the app and submits credentials.
43: - **Main flow:** `POST /api/auth/login` validates email + SHA-256 password hash; returns JWT-style base64 token (`id:role`) and profile.
44: - **Edge flows:** invalid credentials → 401; rate limit of 10 attempts/min/IP → 429.

(End of file - total 44 lines)

203: - **Error codes:**
204:   - `400` — `{ "error": "Provide delegates array, delegateIds, delegateId, or name" }`
205:   - `404` — `{ "error": "Programme not found" }`
206:   - `500` — `{ "error": "<message>" }`
207: 
208: ### 3.3 Update a delegate
209: 
210: - **Method / Path:** `PATCH /delegates/:delegateId`
211: - **Description:** Link or unlink a delegate to a user account.
212: - **Request body:**
213: ```json
214: { "userId": "u1-..." }
215: ```
216: - **Success — `200 OK`:**
217: ```json
218: { "id": "b2c3d4e5-...", "name": "Lim Wei Jie", "userId": "u1-..." }
219: ```
220: - **Error codes:**
221:   - `404` — `{ "error": "Delegate not found" }`
222:   - `400` — `{ "error": "User not found" }` (when `userId` given but invalid)
223:   - `500` — `{ "error": "<message>" }`
224: 
225: ### 3.4 Remove a delegate from a programme
226: 
227: - **Method / Path:** `DELETE /programmes/:id/delegates/:delegateId`
228: - **Description:** Remove a delegate from a programme. Also deletes the delegate's attendance records and route memberships within the programme.
229: - **Success — `204 No Content`**
230: - **Error codes:**
231:   - `404` — `{ "error": "Delegate not found in programme" }`
232:   - `500` — `{ "error": "<message>" }`
233: 
234: ### 3.5 Set a delegate's route membership
235: 
236: - **Method / Path:** `PUT /programmes/:id/delegates/:delegateId/routes`
237: - **Description:** Assign a delegate to exactly one route (or clear their route with an empty array). Enforces the single-route rule.
238: - **Request body:**
239: ```json
240: { "routeIds": ["a1b2c3d4-..."] }
241: ```
242: - **Success — `200 OK`:**
243: ```json
244: { "delegateId": "b2c3d4e5-...", "routeIds": ["a1b2c3d4-..."], "routeNames": ["Coach A"] }
245: ```
246: - **Error codes:**
247:   - `400` — `{ "error": "routeIds must be an array" }`
248:   - `400` — `{ "error": "Each delegate can only be assigned to one route" }`
249:   - `400` — `{ "error": "Invalid routeId: <id>" }`
250:   - `500` — `{ "error": "<message>" }`
251: 
252: ### 3.6 Get a delegate's route membership
253: 
254: - **Method / Path:** `GET /programmes/:id/delegates/:delegateId/routes`
255: - **Description:** Fetch a delegate's current route assignment(s).
256: - **Success — `200 OK`:** same shape as §3.5.
257: - **Error codes:** `500` — `{ "error": "<message>" }`
258: 
259: ---
260: 
261: ## 4. Attendance
262: 
263: ### 4.1 Get attendance
264: 
265: - **Method / Path:** `GET /programmes/:id/attendance`
266: - **Description:** Fetch the full attendance snapshot for a programme: present delegates (with method and check-in time), missing delegates, and unidentified scan events.
267: - **Success — `200 OK`:**
268: ```json
269: {
270:   "present": [
271:     { "delegateId": "b2c3d4e5-...", "name": "Lim Wei Jie", "routeId": "a1b2c3d4-...", "routeName": "Coach A", "routeIds": ["a1b2c3d4-..."], "routeNames": ["Coach A"], "method": "manual", "checkedInAt": "2026-08-10T09:12:33.000Z", "notes": "" }
272:   ],
273:   "missing": [
274:     { "delegateId": "c3d4e5f6-...", "name": "Tan Mei Ling", "routeId": null, "routeName": null, "routeIds": [], "routeNames": [], "notes": "" }
275:   ],
276:   "unidentified": [ { "scanId": "e5f6a7b8-...", "scannedAt": "2026-08-10T09:13:00.000Z" } ]
277: }
278: ```
279: - **Error codes:** `500` — `{ "error": "<message>" }`
280: 
281: ### 4.2 Mark a delegate's attendance
282: 
283: - **Method / Path:** `PUT /programmes/:id/attendance/:delegateId`
284: - **Description:** Mark a single delegate present or absent. On success, an `attendance:updated` WebSocket event is broadcast to all staff devices in the programme room.
285: - **Request body:**
286: ```json
287: { "status": "present", "method": "manual", "notes": "badge missing, verified by photo" }
288: ```
289: - **Success — `200 OK`:**
290: ```json
291: { "programmeId": "f47ac10b-...", "delegateId": "b2c3d4e5-...", "name": "Lim Wei Jie", "status": "present", "method": "manual", "checkedInAt": "2026-08-10T09:12:33.000Z" }
292: ```
293: - **Error codes:**
294:   - `400` — `{ "error": "status must be \"present\" or \"absent\"" }`
295:   - `400` — `{ "error": "method is required when marking present" }`
296:   - `400` — `{ "error": "Delegate is not in this programme" }`
297:   - `500` — `{ "error": "<message>" }`
298: 
299: ### 4.3 Batch mark attendance
300: 
301: - **Method / Path:** `POST /programmes/:id/attendance`
302: - **Description:** Mark attendance for multiple delegates in one request. Each record is processed independently.
303: - **Request body:**
304: ```json
305: { "records": [ { "delegateId": "b2c3d4e5-...", "status": "present", "method": "manual" }, { "delegateId": "c3d4e5f6-...", "status": "absent" } ] }
306: ```
307: - **Success — `200 OK`** (when at least one record fails) or **`201 Created`** (all succeeded):
308: ```json
309: { "success": [ { "programmeId": "...", "delegateId": "...", "name": "...", "status": "present", "method": "manual", "checkedInAt": "..." } ], "errors": [ { "delegateId": "...", "error": "..." } ] }
310: ```
311: - **Error codes:**
312:   - `400` — `{ "error": "records must be a non-empty array" }` (also returned when all records fail)
313:   - `500` — `{ "error": "<message>" }`
314: 
315: ### 4.4 Get attendance summary
316: 
317: - **Method / Path:** `GET /programmes/:id/attendance/summary`
318: - **Description:** Fetch aggregate attendance for the programme, broken down per route, plus the count of unidentified scans.
319: - **Success — `200 OK`:**
320: ```json
321: {
322:   "total": 32, "checkedIn": 27, "missing": 5, "unidentified": 2,
323:   "unidentifiedScans": [ { "scanId": "e5f6a7b8-...", "scannedAt": "2026-08-10T09:13:00.000Z" } ],
324:   "byRoute": [
325:     { "routeId": "a1b2c3d4-...", "routeName": "Coach A", "total": 16, "checkedIn": 14, "missing": 2, "unidentified": 1 }
326:   ]
327: }
328: ```
329: - **Error codes:** `500` — `{ "error": "<message>" }`
330: 
331: ---
332: 
333: ## 5. Ready-to-Depart
334: 
335: ### 5.1 Get ready-to-depart status
336: 
337: - **Method / Path:** `GET /programmes/:id/routes/:routeId/ready-to-depart`
338: - **Description:** Fetch the ready-to-depart status for a route.
339: - **Success — `200 OK`:**
340: ```json
341: { "routeId": "a1b2c3d4-...", "ready": false, "toggledBy": null, "toggledAt": null }
342: ```
343: - **Error codes:** `500` — `{ "error": "<message>" }`
344: 
345: ### 5.2 Toggle ready-to-depart
346: 
347: - **Method / Path:** `PUT /programmes/:id/routes/:routeId/ready-to-depart`
348: - **Description:** Set whether a route is ready to depart.
349: - **Request body:**
350: ```json
351: { "ready": true }
352: ```
353: - **Success — `200 OK`:**
354: ```json
355: { "routeId": "a1b2c3d4-...", "ready": true, "toggledBy": null, "toggledAt": "2026-08-10T09:20:00.000Z" }
356: ```
357: - **Error codes:**
358:   - `400` — `{ "error": "ready must be a boolean" }`
359:   - `500` — `{ "error": "<message>" }`
360: 
361: ---
362: 
363: ## 6. Shared Error Codes
364: 
365: | Code | Meaning |
366: |------|---------|
367: | `200` | OK — request succeeded |
368: | `201` | Created — a new resource was created |
369: | `204` | No Content — deletion succeeded, no body returned |
370: | `400` | Bad Request — invalid/missing body fields or a validation rule failed |
371: | `404` | Not Found — the resource (programme/route/delegate) does not exist |
372: | `429` | Too Many Requests — rate-limited (applies to `/sync` and `/api/auth/login`; not the programme routes) |
373: | `500` | Internal Server Error — unexpected server failure; body is `{ "error": "<message>" }` |
374: 
375: Error responses always use the shape `{ "error": "<human-readable message>" }`.
